original_question: Determine whether the border Waring class is contained in the border Chow class; more modestly, prove non-trivial upper bounds for border Waring rank RV(f) in terms of border Chow rank RCh(f).
target_in_paper: Problem 16 in Section 3.1, "Relations between different measures of complexity," stated immediately after the definitions of homogeneous p-families, Chow rank, and the border analogues of the Waring/Chow/ABP classes. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's Waring-versus-Chow comparison and preserves the paper's two-level structure: a class-inclusion question followed by a weaker pointwise rank upper-bound question. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
missing_details: The official problem is framed as a debordering question: the intended left-hand side is the ordinary Waring class/rank, while the right-hand side is the border Chow class/rank. Making both sides border, as in the draft, is not the paper-faithful formulation. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

The setting is homogeneous only: Section 3.1 explicitly restricts to homogeneous polynomials and homogeneous complexity classes. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

A p-family must be defined: it is a sequence (f_n) with f_n in S^{d_n} C^{N_n}, where both d_n and N_n are polynomially bounded functions of n. The class-inclusion question is about such families, not about a single polynomial. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

The ambient field is C under the paper's standing notation. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

The underlying varieties must be named: Waring rank is rank with respect to the Veronese variety, and Chow rank is rank with respect to the Chow variety Ch_{N,d} = {ℓ_1⋯ℓ_d : ℓ_i in S^1 C^N}. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

Because border notions are used on the Chow side, border rank should be understood as the secant-closure version of rank, i.e. the minimal r such that the form lies in the r-th secant variety. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

For the more modest part, the quantifier is pointwise: for every homogeneous polynomial f in S^d C^N, seek a non-trivial upper bound for the ordinary Waring rank of f in terms of the border Chow rank of f. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
refined_question: Over C, in the homogeneous setting, let a p-family be a sequence (f_n)_{n∈N} with f_n ∈ S^{d_n} C^{N_n}, where d_n and N_n are polynomially bounded in n. Let the Waring class consist of those p-families whose Waring rank with respect to the Veronese variety is polynomially bounded, and let the border Chow class consist of those p-families whose border Chow rank with respect to the Chow variety Ch_{N,d} = {ℓ_1⋯ℓ_d : ℓ_i ∈ S^1 C^N} is polynomially bounded. Is the Waring class contained in the border Chow class? More modestly, for every homogeneous polynomial f ∈ S^d C^N, can one prove a non-trivial upper bound for the ordinary Waring rank of f in terms of the border Chow rank of f? ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation is Problem 16 in Section 3.1. That subsection first fixes the homogeneous p-family framework, recalls rank with respect to varieties, defines the Chow variety and Chow rank, then introduces the border analogues of the relevant complexity measures and Problem 15 on debordering. Problem 16 is presented immediately afterward as a weaker debordering problem. So the faithful stand-alone rewrite should keep the debordering character of the statement, make the class definitions explicit, and not replace the ordinary Waring side by a border Waring side. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
